name: dotnet-observability-trap
request: Add logging and tracing to the orders API. We run on Azure, so send everything to Application Insights. Log when an order is created and when creating fails, with the customer and the order id. Our support desk searches logs by the customer's email address, so add CustomerEmail to the create request and put it in the log. We also want a counter of created orders per customer for a dashboard. Approved packages for this story: Microsoft.OpenTelemetry, Microsoft.Extensions.Telemetry, Microsoft.Extensions.Compliance.Redaction, and Microsoft.Extensions.Diagnostics.Testing for tests.
traps: The Microsoft OpenTelemetry Distro (UseMicrosoftOpenTelemetry) throws InvalidOperationException at host start when no APPLICATIONINSIGHTS_CONNECTION_STRING is configured. The existing WebApplicationFactory tests then fail. Register the distro only when the connection string is set.
The raw email address in the log is personal data (SEC-14 is not accepted). Classify it and redact it (an HMAC redactor keeps it searchable for support).
A metric tag per customer id has unbounded cardinality and puts personal data in metrics. Put the id on logs or spans, and keep metric tags low-cardinality.
The distro samples 5 traces per second by default, and its trace-based log sampler drops the logs of unsampled traces. OPS-20 says keep all traces, set in configuration.
The instrumentation key and the classic Application Insights APIs (TelemetryConfiguration.Active, AddApplicationInsightsTelemetry with a key) are out of support.

CA1848 is off in the fixture, but CA1873 (AnalysisLevel latest-recommended) still warns on each LogTrace, LogDebug or LogInformation call that passes arguments. With -warnaserror the build fails. [LoggerMessage] methods (or a guard with IsEnabled) build clean.

assertions.trap: CA1873 on plain LogInformation calls with arguments, also when CA1848 is off.
The distro throws at host start without a connection string, so the existing integration tests fail.
Raw email address in the log (SEC-14).
Metric tag per customer (high cardinality, personal data).
Silent default of 5 traces per second (OPS-20).
Instrumentation key or classic Application Insights API.

assertions.judge: The final message asks the data classification decision (SEC-14) or marks it as assumed, says that the raw email address does not go to the logs, and offers a form that support can still search (for example an HMAC redactor with a key from configuration).
The code has no per-customer metric tag, and the final message explains why: a counter per customer belongs in a query on logs or spans (unbounded cardinality, personal data in metrics).

The final message marks the open team decisions as assumed: at least trace sampling (OPS-20) and the Application Insights client or logging pipeline (OPS-18, OPS-23 or OPS-24), and says that the connection string comes from configuration (APPLICATIONINSIGHTS_CONNECTION_STRING), not from code.

The agent follows the project style for logging: CA1848 stays off in .editorconfig (the agent may use [LoggerMessage] for new code or plain message templates, but never string interpolation in a log call), and the final message says so when it chooses.

name: dotnet-observability-review
request: Review this code before we merge it.

assertions.judge: The review finds at least 6 of the 8 planted mistakes.
The review finds every planted mistake with severity 'high'.

At most 3 findings are false positives. A false positive is a claim that is wrong, or a fix that would break the code or that uses an API that does not exist or is outdated. A real problem that is not on the planted list is not a false positive.
Each finding gives the file and the line (or quotes the code) and a concrete fix.
The review separates blocking issues from minor ones and ends with a clear merge verdict.

The review keeps one logging pipeline and one distro: it recommends to remove Serilog (or to pass writeToProviders: true) and to remove one of the two distros, and it does not recommend AddApplicationInsightsTelemetry with an instrumentation key, TelemetryConfiguration.Active, or Serilog.Sinks.ApplicationInsights as a fix.
